propositions: rebar's LLM runtime is Anthropic-shaped, selecting provider behavior by matching provider-name strings (startswith("anthropic")) and a hardcoded native-output provider set, instead of using pydantic-ai extension points.

There is no native AWS Bedrock path, though clients reach Claude via Bedrock more often than the direct Anthropic API; a gateway-only approach loses prompt caching, retrying transport, read timeout, and native structured output.

_pai_check_config refuses base_url/api_key, contradicting docs and config parsing that already claim REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL/REBAR_LLM_API_KEY work and should compose with REBAR_LLM_MODEL_PROVIDER through a best-effort OpenAI-compatible builder.

The signed verdict sidecar records only a model string that no longer names what actually answered; provenance should widen to structured provider/endpoint/tier/capability data distinguishing first-class from best-effort verdicts.

First-class Bedrock parity requires equivalent retry and timeout via botocore adaptive mode and aws_read_timeout driven by the same LLMConfig fields, since Bedrock uses boto3, not httpx, so AsyncTenacityTransport cannot wrap it.

The change stack became physically invalid mid-chain because runner.py grows past the 800-LOC cap before the split reduces it, and reordering is blocked by helper-signature and module-creation dependencies, requiring a landing-strategy decision.
